newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tryg-Baltica sees lower full year profits.
newsitem.headline: Tryg-Baltica sees lower full year profits.

text.p: Danish insurance group Tryg-Baltica posted on Wednesday lower first-half 1996 profits hit by unsatisfactory core activity earnings and forecast full year profits lower than in 1995.

"The profit for the (interim) period reflects a not fully satisfactory profit on core insurance operations in non-life business and a financial return which was affected by large capital gains," Tryg-Baltica, Denmark's biggest insurer, said in a statement accompanying its half-year 1996 result.
Tryg-Baltica posted a 381 million crown ($66.7 million) net profit for 1996's first six months.

This figure compared with the same 1995 period's 557 million crowns and the insurer forecast net profits for the full year in the 550-600 million crown range, based on securities rates at end-June 1996.
In March, the insurer returned to 1.060 billion crown net profit for whole year 1995 after reporting a 556 million crown loss in the previous year.

It said its interim 1996 profit provided a return on equity of 12.5 percent, with shareholders' equity totalling 6.3 billion crowns at end-June, exceeding Denmark's statutory solvency requirement by almost 3.5 billion crowns.
Tryg-Baltica said premium earnings in the period rose 14 percent since mid-1995 to 4.4 billion crowns, with total non-life premiums up six percent and life premiums 15 percent higher.

It said earned premiums for both non-life and life insurances were expected to increase in 1996's second half and announced that most motor premiums were to go up by an average 10 percent effective October 1.
"The increase in most motor premiums is due to generally high claims in motor insurance, with a claims ratio of close to one hundred in the first six months of the year," it said.

Former Baltica Forsikring and Tryg Forsikring merged in May 1995 to form Denmark's biggest insurance group and the company said that work to fully merge the two firms' insurance administrative systems was well under way.

It said it expected a minor improvement in the combined ratio for the full year compared to 1995's 107 percent but that the technical result would be lower as a result of the falling technical interest rate.
Total assets were put at 57.9 billion crowns at end-June against 52.2 billion a year previously.
The Tryg-Baltica share climbed seven crowns to around 300 immediately after its interim result was announced, slipping back to 294 by 1200 gmt, seven crowns up on the opening.
